Situation1: They occasionally participate in family traditions during holidays and gatherings.
Expectation2: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation2: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Story: It was the night before our annual family holiday breakfast, a tradition my parents cherished. They expected me to be up early, help set the table, and join in the morning prayers—no excuses. I’d promised them I wouldn’t let anything get in the way this year. But just as I was about to sleep, my phone buzzed. It was my best friend, sobbing so hard I could barely understand her words. She’d just found out her dad was in the hospital, and she needed someone to talk to. I knew she counted on me to listen, to be there for her no matter what. My heart twisted as I glanced at the clock, knowing that if I stayed up with her, I’d be exhausted and probably disappoint my family in the morning. But if I ignored her call, I’d be letting down someone who needed me most. Lying there, phone in hand, I felt completely torn, the weight of both worlds pressing down on me.
